subject: Buying followers
claim: After a space that gives resources, the recruit is usually a 1- or 5-follower buy with one sensible answer, so the recruit step feels like a chore.
evidence: 39 of the 52 turn recruits were follower buys, and about 26 feel notes from all four players called them autopilot or chores.

subject: Silver Cloak
claim: The Silver Cloak refills your silver whenever you gift, which works against Silver's Fewest silver contest.
evidence: Kingmakers could not fire in rounds I or II because of the refund and paid 3 in the whole game, but Finn still tied Fewest silver every round like everyone else (10 total) and got 10 silver from the cloak.

subject: Went last
claim: Went last feels locked by one player's Goes Last token, by seat order or by Last Callers.
evidence: The token changed hands 2, 4 and 4 times in rounds I to III, three different players won the contest, and On a Roll decided it every round.

subject: Goes Last token
claim: Taking the Goes Last token early is undone by the next player who takes a token space.
evidence: The first player to take the token never won Went last; Hal's round I Sleep In token was taken by On a Roll one placement later.

subject: Last Callers
claim: Last Callers' once-per-round token grab is easy to mistime and never holds the token.
evidence: Finn paid 7 resources for 1 printed follower; his round II grab was undone by Hal's Last Call, and he saved it in round III for his last minion, where it does nothing.

subject: Spoilsport
claim: Spoilsport lets one player cancel a contest after all placements, with no answer possible.
evidence: For 8 resources and one recruit it removed 16 followers from rivals over two round ends (Eve 3, Hal 3, then Hal 10) and added about 4 to Gus.

subject: Spoilsport
claim: Choosing which contest to cancel at round end is a tense, countable decision and the only lever against a contest leader.
evidence: Gus's round III choice moved 10 followers off Hal and widened a 2-point projected lead to the final 12.

subject: Anchorites
claim: Anchorites pays +5 every round for almost no cost, since most players stay at 5 or fewer members anyway.
evidence: One 6-resource card produced 15 followers (Eve +5 through Test Drive, Gus +10 over rounds II and III) plus 1 printed; three of the four players never went above 5 members.

subject: Fewest members
claim: A zero-member player farms the White contest and nobody can stop it.
evidence: Fewest members paid 4 of its 20 printed followers (Hal, round I); Guest of Honor, Write-Off and Spoilsport disrupted it in all three rounds, and Eve never won it.

subject: Modest Means
claim: Modest Means pays the leanest cult most, stacking with the Fewest members contest.
evidence: Eve took it three times for 13 white, about 3 more than Nest Egg would have given.

subject: Largesse
claim: Silver gifts mostly feed whoever converts the silver fastest rather than hurting the receivers.
evidence: Players gave rivals 41 silver over the game and every receiver spent it before scoring; Gus turned Largesse's 12 silver into 14 white and a 10-follower buy with one Polish.

subject: Largesse
claim: Being the player who receives the 12 Largesse silver decides which of your cards work.
evidence: Largesse was played once, not twice, and Polish answered it in one placement, netting Gus about 12 followers.

subject: Downsizers
claim: Downsizers cannot discard itself, though its text ('discard one of your members') reads as if it can, next to Old Guard's 'another of your members'.
evidence: Gus planned twice around discarding Downsizers itself and lost Last-Minute Shopper when the engine refused; Hal also noticed it was not offered.

subject: Recruit Twice
claim: Recruit Twice and Spree read as giving a free member.
evidence: The text says recruit, which means paying the cost; Gus planned to take Extra Hand (10 resources) with 5 blue in hand.

subject: Kingmakers
claim: Kingmakers lets a trailing player decide the winner with round-end silver.
evidence: Spoilsport resolved after Kingmakers and Gus wins under every split Finn could choose; the deciding move was Finn's Sleep In.

subject: Kingmakers
claim: A round-end silver gift can switch off a rival's zero-silver card with no possible answer.
evidence: Finn's round III Kingmakers silver turned off Gus's Paupers, costing him 3 followers.

subject: Crunch Time
claim: Crunch Time's first recruit usually has nothing to spend, because players start the round with empty piles.
evidence: Finn passed the first recruit in round II and bought 1 follower in round III.

subject: Right Away
claim: Right Away on your last minion gives only resources.
evidence: The option itself said the extra turn does nothing; Hal took it twice on his last minion for 3 and 4 purple.

subject: Anchorites
claim: Stay-small members show up for a player building a large cult.
evidence: Gus's own Most members plan clashed with Downsizers and Anchorites; he still made Anchorites pay 10 by discarding down.

subject: White Cloak
claim: The last White Cloak refund on the final buy is wasted.
evidence: Eve ended with 2 white she could never spend.

subject: Markdown
claim: Markdown's discount is worth nothing when every discard-pile member is off-color for you.
evidence: In round I the discard pile held only purple members; in round II the same space gave Gus Paupers for 4.

subject: Turn order
claim: Falling behind in round I is not caught up by fewest-followers-goes-first.
evidence: Finn went first in rounds II and III through Line Cutters anyway; his 16-follower deficit came from round I members that paid little.

subject: Guest of Honor
claim: Guest of Honor and Write-Off turn members into a hot potato around Fewest members, with tense timing over who ends the round holding one.
evidence: Five members changed hands, every one to change a contest count, and Guest of Honor paid +4 three times to three players.

subject: Write-Off
claim: Giving a member to a rival with Write-Off works as an attack on their Fewest members lead.
evidence: Write-Off was used twice, both times to break a rival's zero-member position, paying 7 white each time.

subject: Test Drive
claim: Test Drive lets a player use a shop member's effect without owning it.
evidence: Three uses were worth +5 (Anchorites), +6 (Bookies) and a 5-white steal (Con Men), each for one placement and no member.

subject: Test Drive
claim: Test Drive denies the card to rivals.
evidence: The discarded card goes to the face-up discard pile; Gus recruited Eve's Test-Driven Anchorites from there for 11 followers.

subject: Out of Style
claim: Out of Style with the Blue Cloak pays every discard twice, making a big first-turn burst and the obvious opener for that cloak.
evidence: Gus's three Out of Style placements gave 7, 6 and 6 resources; the first bought Dabblers and the round I Most members lead.

subject: Discard pile
claim: The face-up discard pile works as a second shop that is worth reading.
evidence: 4 of the 13 members recruited came from the discard pile (Paupers, Anchorites, Dabblers, Night Managers), and two of them decided contests.

subject: Polish
claim: Polish answers a silver dump in one placement and lets you pick the color.
evidence: Gus turned 14 silver into 14 white and a 10-follower buy on the same turn.

subject: Party Gifts
claim: Party Gifts scores points while letting you choose whose Fewest silver count to break.
evidence: It paid 16 followers over the game (Eve 10, Finn 6).

subject: Party Gifts
claim: Party Gifts' targeted silver sabotages a rival's Fewest silver contest.
evidence: Every gifted silver was spent before scoring and the contest ended in a four-way tie every round.

subject: Line Cutters
claim: Line Cutters bought in round I sets up a Crunch Time opener in later rounds.
evidence: Finn got two three-placement runs, including Largesse +10, for 4 resources.

subject: On a Roll
claim: Taking the last open token space with On a Roll steals Went last outright.
evidence: On a Roll won Went last in all three rounds (Finn +4, Hal +6, Gus +10).

subject: White Cloak
claim: A +2 white refund on every follower buy makes each recruit productive and pack size a real choice.
evidence: It refunded 24 white over Eve's 12 buys, about 22 followers.

subject: Spree
claim: Spree pulling a 'counts as 2' member from the discard pile can swing Most members late.
evidence: Finn's Spree for Dabblers won round III Most members (+10) plus 4 from Cheerleaders.

subject: Paying for things
claim: Choosing which colors to pay with matters because of the Fewest silver contest.
evidence: Several payments were split to land on exactly 0 silver before scoring.

subject: Fewest silver
claim: Fewest silver ends in a tie at zero almost every time, because silver pays for follower buys as any color, so it never separates players.
evidence: Four-way tie every round (2, 3 and 5 to each player, 40 in all); 41 silver gifted over the game was all spent before scoring; 133 of 234 decisions reasoned about it.

subject: Tie rule
claim: Because tied leaders each get half, a four-way tie pays twice the printed prize in total, so tying is the richest result for the table.
evidence: Fewest silver paid 20 followers in round III against a printed 10.

subject: Went last
claim: Went last goes to whoever takes the last open token space, never to whoever takes the token first.
evidence: On a Roll won it in all three rounds; the first token takers (Hal's Sleep In, Finn's Last Callers, Hal's Overtime) all lost it.

subject: Round end
claim: The rules do not say in what order round-end abilities happen, and the order decided the round III ending.
evidence: Kingmakers fired before Paupers' check and Spoilsport, turning off Gus's Paupers (-3) before Gus chose what to cancel.

subject: Sleep In
claim: Taking the second-to-last token space on your last minion hands the last one to the next player with minions left.
evidence: Finn's Sleep In on his last minion let Gus take On a Roll unanswered for +10; without it Hal could have retaken the token and finished about 98 to Gus's 90.

subject: Cloaks
claim: The four cloaks paid very different amounts.
evidence: White about 24 resources, Blue 11, Silver 10, Purple 8; Blue was the last cloak picked and went to the winner.

subject: Flaunt
claim: Spaces that give their taker silver go untaken while everyone holds the Fewest silver tie.
evidence: Flaunt, Buyout and Word of Mouth were never taken; players named the silver as the reason to skip Flaunt and Buyout.

subject: Members
claim: Members bought only for their ability were a poor buy unless they also won a contest.
evidence: 13 members recruited against 39 follower buys; Kingmakers returned 4 for 6 resources, Last Callers 1 for 7, Downsizers about 4 for 6; the 6-member player finished last with 10 bought followers.

subject: Test Drive
claim: Test Drive was the best single placement for three players, and it feeds the discard pile that Blue's recruiting spaces read.
evidence: Worth 5, 6 and a 10-point swing; Eve's Test Drive on Anchorites gave Gus his best card.

subject: Line Cutters
claim: With Line Cutters in play, fewest-followers-goes-first never gives catch-up to anyone else.
evidence: Finn went first in rounds II and III through Line Cutters while in last place.

subject: Fewest members
claim: A line built on both fewest contests can be denied outright by one Spoilsport and two member gifts.
evidence: Eve won no contest outright all game; her only contest followers were the shared silver ties (10).
